# Exercise 1: Sampling & Seeds (Cycle 1)

```{r}
#| label: ex1-data
patient_ids <- 101:115
participants <- 1:16
clinics <- c("Bellevue", "Elmhurst", "Harlem", "Jacobi", "Kings County",
             "Lincoln", "Metropolitan", "North Central Bronx", "Queens",
             "Coney Island", "Woodhull", "Gouverneur")
```

```{r}
#| label: ex1-sampling
```

# Exercise 2: Probability Distributions (Cycle 2)

```{r}
#| label: ex2-distributions
# 1. Systolic BP (SBP) is normal with mean 125 and SD 15.
#    (a) What share of adults has SBP >= 140? (pnorm)
#    (b) What is the 95th percentile of SBP? (qnorm)
# 2. After set.seed(2182), simulate 5,000 SBP values with rnorm() and compare
#    the simulated share >= 140 with your answer to 1(a)
# 3. 25 patients each take their medication with probability 0.8.
#    (a) P(exactly 20 take it)  (b) P(at least 22 take it)
#    Hint: "at least 22" is 1 minus "at most 21"
# 4. A hospital ward averages 2.5 falls per week (Poisson).
#    (a) P(no falls in a week)  (b) P(more than 5 falls in a week)

```

# Exercise 3: Monte Carlo: ER Surge Risk (Cycle 3)

An emergency room averages 6 arrivals per hour and can handle 9 per hour.

```{r}
#| label: ex3-montecarlo
# 1. Write surge_hours(n_hours = 8, rate = 6, capacity = 9) that simulates ONE
#    shift with rpois(n_hours, lambda = rate) and returns the number of hours
#    whose arrivals are above capacity
# 2. After set.seed(2182), run 5,000 shifts with map_dbl() and store the results
# 3. Estimate (a) P(at least one surge hour in a shift) and
#    (b) the mean number of surge hours per shift
# 4. Compare with the exact answers:
#    (a) 1 - ppois(9, 6)^8   (b) 8 * (1 - ppois(9, 6))
#    How close is each estimate? What happens with only 100 shifts?

```

# Exercise 4: The Central Limit Theorem + AI Corner (Cycle 4)

Hospital length of stay is skewed: model it as exponential with a mean of 4 days (`rate = 1 / 4`).

```{r}
#| label: ex4-clt

#    Which panel looks closer to a normal curve?
# 3. For each n, compare sd(xbar) with the theory value 4 / sqrt(n)
```
